To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the project identification process is a decision-making process; (ii) decision-making is a process of rationality; (iii) rationality is a function of the decision-maker; (iv) the decision-maker's perception is a function of his/her values; and (v) values are a function of the socio-economic and cultural environment of the decision-maker.

(1) the identification of farmers' problems is the key to the design of effective agricultural development projects; (2) the current approach to the identification of problems is inadequate; and (3) a new approach is needed.
project identification is a process that is not well understood and that is not adequately addressed in the literature, and that it is a process that can be greatly improved.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the way projects are generated in agricultural development.
how to improve the project identification process.
how the project identification process can be improved.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the project cycle is a poor instrument for project identification.
the current approach to the identification process in agricultural projects should be replaced by a decision paradigm.

the project identification process should be improved by: a) a more thorough understanding of the decision process and the role of decision-makers; b) the use of more rigorous and systematic methods; and c) a better understanding of the nature of the problem and its causes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the current approach to agricultural project design and evaluation is inadequate, and that the project identification process should be improved by the introduction of a new decision paradigm.
we are not so concerned with the ‘what’ of project identification as we are with the ‘how’ of project identification.
the identification process should be more participatory and more analytical.
The main takeaway from our work is that

a new approach is needed, which takes account of the fact that farmers are the ultimate users and beneficiaries of agricultural development, and that they must be involved in the project identification process.
the identification of projects should involve a more systematic and scientific approach to the collection and interpretation of data.
the current approach to the identification of development projects needs to be changed to take into account the decision-making processes of the key actors.
